test_stimuli.name: ch0_mid_scale
test_stimuli.derivation: For CH0: response bytes [0x00, 0x80, 0x00]; high_byte=0x80, low_byte=0x00; raw = ((0x80 & 0x03) << 8) | 0x00 = (0 << 8) | 0 = 0. Wait, that gives 0. Let's recalc: high_byte=0x80, low_byte=0x00; raw = ((0x80 & 0x03) * 256) + 0x00 = (0 * 256) + 0 = 0. That's not 512. Need different bytes. Choose response [0x00, 0xA0, 0x00] for CH0: high_byte=0xA0, low_byte=0x00; raw = ((0xA0 & 0x03) * 256) + 0x00 = (0 * 256) + 0 = 0. Still 0. Actually, the ADC output is 10 bits: bits 9:8 in byte1[1:0], bits 7:0 in byte2. For raw=512 (binary 10 0000 0000), byte1[1:0]=10 (0x02), byte2=0x00. So response bytes: [0x00, 0x80, 0x00] gives byte1=0x80, byte1[1:0]=0x00, byte2=0x00 => raw=0. To get raw=512, need byte1=0x80|0x02=0x82, byte2=0x00. So response [0x00, 0x82, 0x00]. Then raw = ((0x82 & 0x03) * 256) + 0x00 = (2 * 256) + 0 = 512. For CH1, not read in this stimulus, so expected 0.

test_stimuli.name: ch1_full_scale
test_stimuli.derivation: For CH1: response bytes [0x00, 0x83, 0xFF]; high_byte=0x83, low_byte=0xFF; raw = ((0x83 & 0x03) * 256) + 0xFF = (3 * 256) + 255 = 768 + 255 = 1023. CH0 not read, expected 0.

test_stimuli.name: ch0_zero
test_stimuli.derivation: For CH0: response bytes [0x00, 0x80, 0x00]; high_byte=0x80, low_byte=0x00; raw = ((0x80 & 0x03) * 256) + 0x00 = (0 * 256) + 0 = 0. CH1 not read, expected 0.
